name: Perseus
introduction: is the hero who beheaded Medusa and rescued Andromeda from the sea monster. He stands in the Milky Way between Cassiopeia and Taurus, holding Medusa’s head, marked by the winking star Algol. It is best seen on northern autumn and winter evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: [Algol](hip:14576), the Demon Star, dims noticeably every 2 days and 21 hours, for about ten hours, when a fainter companion passes in front of its brighter star. It was one of the first eclipsing binaries understood, and it poses a puzzle: the less massive star is more evolved, because it has lost much of its mass to its partner.
Every August, the Perseids, one of the best meteor showers of the year, radiate from Perseus. They are debris from Comet Swift–Tuttle.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Mirfak](hip:15863), the brightest star, is a yellow-white supergiant surrounded by the Alpha Persei Cluster, a loose group of young stars easily seen in binoculars.

[Zeta Persei](hip:18246) and [Epsilon Persei](hip:18532) are blue giants of a young stellar association. [Menkib](hip:18614) is a hot, runaway O-type star that lights up the California Nebula. [Gorgonea Tertia](hip:14354), near Algol, is a pulsating red giant.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The Double Cluster, two rich open clusters side by side, is visible to the naked eye between Perseus and Cassiopeia. The [Perseus Molecular Cloud](id:cahlon-cloud-6) is forming new stars, and [Sh 2-216](id:sh-2-216), about 400 light-years away, is one of the nearest planetary nebulae. Far beyond, the Perseus Cluster of galaxies surrounds NGC 1275, whose black hole emits sound waves in the hot gas, about 57 octaves below middle C.
